answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must keep a falcon-class sentinel process resident, answering unpredictable liveness probes at a bounded rate; missed windows decay its score below the posting threshold. Because probes arrive only to a live process holding a slot, an attacker must pay real compute and near-continuous operator attention per identity, not one-time registration. Duplicates starve: sustaining many across the horizon multiplies idle cycles and fallback audits. A quiet haven of dormant clones earns nothing and cannot recover without fresh work.
